content:
jen_peopleops: quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A — consolidating a few manager questions about promos, retro pay, and comp so it's easy to share.
kate_eng_mgr: thanks! our managers asked: what exactly triggers retro pay and how long until payroll reflects it?
sam_total_rewards: TL;DR: retro pay is to the effective date, not approval date. If promo packet is approved before payroll cutoff for the upcoming pay run, retro appears in that next run; otherwise it hits the following run. Expect a 1-pay-period lag if missed.
jen_peopleops: question: if a manager leaves mid-approval who signs?
arun_ceo: skip-level or director should sign; if both unavailable, People Ops will sign to avoid blocking payroll. Add a note in the packet describing the sign-off path.
omar_engineer: what about people on parental leave — can they be promoted while away?
sam_total_rewards: yes, promotions can be effective during leave. Managers should include prior work examples or cross-team endorsements in the packet; calibration may ask for extra context.
jen_peopleops: short manager checklist to paste into packets:
- employee name, proposed title & band
- effective date (YYYY-MM-DD) + "retro requested" flag if needed
- 2-3 concrete examples of impact
- proposed comp (base + bonus target) and justification
- signer (skip-level if applicable)
- links to supporting docs
jen_peopleops: short 1-line announcement managers can use: "Congrats <name> — you're promoted to <new title> effective <date>. Payroll and People Ops will share next steps; reach out with questions."
people-ops-bot: Promo packet template v4 uploaded: https://drive.google.com/example-promo-v4 (auto-message)
jen_peopleops: i'll publish a 1-pager in #managers by EOD with the checklist, script, and template link. booking two 20-min office hours for packet walk-throughs next week. ping here if you hit an unusual edge case and we'll triage.
